items.t: Nucor (NUE) Could Be 16% Undervalued Following Steady Fourth Quarter Guidance
sum: Nucor (NUE) issued fresh guidance pointing to fourth quarter earnings that are expected to match or slightly exceed third quarter levels, giving investors new context for the stock after recent price volatility.

Recent trading has been choppy for Nucor, with the share price declining 10.6% over the past week and 10.2% over 3 months, even as the year to date share price return sits at 44.6% and the 1 year total shareholder return is 71.7%. This suggests that long term momentum remains strong despite shorter term pressure around sector wide moves and the latest guidance.

Nucor has just dropped sharply after issuing guidance that still points to steady earnings. The real tension is whether that pullback already offers enough cushion, or if patience wins when you look at the valuation next.

Nucor last closed at $244.97, while the most followed valuation framework pins fair value around $291.88, implying a meaningful gap that the latest guidance has not closed. That sets up a story where future capacity, product mix and cash generation do much of the heavy lifting in the model.

Nucor's multi year capital program of roughly $15b to $20b, with several mills and downstream assets already EBITDA positive and capital expenditure guiding to about $2.5b in 2026, is moving from the build phase toward cash generation, which can support higher earnings and free cash flow.
Still, the story can change quickly if nonresidential or infrastructure demand softens, or if execution issues at new mills drag on margins longer than expected.

If the mix of enthusiasm and caution around Nucor feels familiar, treat that as your cue to dig into the details yourself and move quickly to frame your own stance. To weigh both sides in one place, start with the 3 key rewards and 1 important warning sign.

Nucor stock: Q3 profit more than doubles as Q4 outlook holds
sum: Nucor reported a sharp increase in third-quarter earnings on October 26, with stronger steel prices and volumes lifting results across its main operating segments. The company also kept its fourth-quarter earnings outlook broadly steady.

Nucor's investor release said net earnings attributable to stockholders reached 1.32 billion US dollars in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 607 million US dollars a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share rose to 5.80 US dollars from 2.63 US dollars, while net sales increased to 11.25 billion US dollars from 8.52 billion US dollars.

The steel mills segment benefited from higher average selling prices and increased volumes. Steel products also delivered higher earnings on stronger volumes and realized pricing, while the raw materials segment weakened on lower pricing and shipments.

Nucor's EBITDA reached 2.28 billion US dollars in the quarter, compared with 1.27 billion US dollars a year earlier. The company also generated 2.66 billion US dollars of free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026 and returned about 1.36 billion US dollars to stockholders during that period.

Management expects consolidated fourth-quarter earnings to be generally in line with or modestly higher than the third quarter. Higher realized pricing is expected to offset seasonally lower volumes and higher costs in the steel mills business. Steel products earnings are expected to remain stable, while raw materials earnings may decline slightly because of lower direct-reduced-iron pricing.

Growth projects are moving closer to production. Nucor reported the first heat at its West Virginia sheet mill in September and the start-up of a second galvanizing line at its Berkeley, South Carolina, facility. Those investments should expand capabilities, although start-up and operating costs remain relevant to near-term margins.

sum: Nucor Corporation reported net earnings attributable to stockholders of USD 1.32 billion for the third quarter ended October 3, 2026, compared with USD 607 million a year earlier. The steelmaker also posted net sales of USD 11.25 billion, up 32 percent year over year, according to its third-quarter results release. Diluted earnings per share increased to USD 5.80 from USD 2.63.

Nucor said stronger average selling prices and higher volumes supported the quarter. External sales tons reached 7.533 million, 11 percent above the year-earlier period, while the external average sales price per ton rose 19 percent to USD 1,493. EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, increased to USD 2.279 billion from USD 1.265 billion.

The steel mills segment reported earnings before income taxes and noncontrolling interests of USD 1.788 billion, up from USD 793 million in the third quarter of 2025. Nucor attributed the improvement to higher average selling prices and increased volumes, partly offset by higher costs of products sold.

Steel products earnings rose to USD 465 million from USD 319 million as volumes and average realized pricing increased. Raw materials earnings reached USD 105 million, compared with USD 43 million a year earlier, although the segment declined from the second quarter because of lower pricing and shipments. The second-quarter comparison also included USD 130 million in cash refunds linked to earlier raw-material procurement costs.

Chief Executive Officer Leon Topalian said robust demand across key end markets supported the result. He also pointed to the first heat at Nucor's West Virginia sheet mill in September and the start-up of a second galvanizing line at Nucor Steel Berkeley as milestones in the company's capacity expansion.

Nucor expects consolidated fourth-quarter earnings to be generally in line with or modestly higher than the third quarter. In steel mills, higher realized pricing is expected to offset seasonally lower volumes and higher costs. Steel products earnings are expected to remain stable, while raw materials earnings should decline slightly because of lower realized direct reduced iron pricing.
The outlook leaves pricing, shipment volumes and project start-up costs as the main near-term variables for investors.

sum: Nucor Corporation's NUE shares have gained 50.1% in the past six months. The company has also outperformed the Zacks Steel Producers industry's 41% rise over the same time frame.

The gains partly reflect Nucor's strong earnings in the second quarter on Steel Mills segment's strength and an upbeat outlook for the third quarter. NUE is benefiting from healthy demand in key markets, actions to expand its production capabilities and higher steel prices.
Let's take a look into the factors that are driving NUE stock.

Nucor remains committed to boosting production capacity, which should drive profitable growth and strengthen its position as a low-cost producer. It is executing a series of growth projects to tap significant end-market demand. Nucor is seeing strong demand from non-residential construction & infrastructure, military & defense, and energy end markets and has a healthy order backlog. The company has already commissioned some of its growth projects with Gallatin and Brandenburg mills, showing strong production and shipment performance.

The construction of the 3,000,000 tons per annum (tpa) sheet mill with a low-cost profile in West Virginia, the company's biggest ongoing project, is expected to be completed in late 2026 within production expected in 2027. The new 500,000 tpa galvanizing line at the Berkeley County sheet mill in South Carolina is also on track. Its third greenfield project in Utah is also on course for production commencement in 2027.

The company has been focusing on growth through strategic acquisitions over the past several years. The recent acquisition of Southwest Data Products expanded its growing portfolio of solutions for data center customers. The buyout of Rytec Corporation will also allow Nucor to further expand beyond its core steelmaking businesses into related downstream businesses. Adding high-performance doors is expected to create cross-selling opportunities with other Nucor businesses and significantly expand its product portfolio for the commercial space.

Higher U.S. steel prices have created a favorable landscape for American steel producers. U.S. steel prices recovered in the fourth quarter of 2025, following the lows seen in the third quarter, and the momentum continues so far this year.

Nucor Announces Guidance for the Third Quarter of 2026 Earnings
sum: CHARLOTTE, N.C., September 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nucor Corporation (NYSE: NUE) today announced guidance for its third quarter ending October 3, 2026. Nucor expects third quarter earnings to be in the range of $5.55 to $5.65 per diluted share. Nucor reported second quarter 2026 net earnings of $5.04 and adjusted net earnings of $4.84, both per diluted share. Nucor reported $2.63 per diluted share in the third quarter of 2025.

Second quarter of 2026 results included a non-cash, pre-tax benefit of $61 million ($0.20 per diluted share) related to the increase in the valuation of our investment in Helion, a fusion energy company.
Third Quarter of 2026 Outlook Compared to the Second Quarter of 2026

Third quarter earnings are expected to increase in the steel mills and steel products segments, while decreasing in the raw materials segment. The expected increase in the steel mills segment is due to higher average selling prices and stable volumes, partially offset by higher costs of products sold. Second quarter steel mills segment earnings benefited from $130 million in cash refunds associated with prior periods' raw material procurement costs, and we do not expect a similar benefit in the third quarter. In the steel products segment, we expect increased earnings due to higher volumes and higher average realized pricing. Raw materials segment earnings are expected to decline on lower pricing and shipments.

We expect higher corporate/eliminations expense in the third quarter, reflecting both the absence of the Helion valuation adjustment, and intersegment profit eliminations in line with the prior quarter.

During the third quarter, Nucor has repurchased approximately 2.03 million shares at an average price of $247.04 per share. Nucor has returned approximately $1.36 billion to stockholders in the form of share repurchases and dividend payments year-to-date.

Nucor plans to release its earnings after the markets close on Monday, October 26, 2026, and will host a conference call the morning of Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time to review the Company's third quarter results. The event will be broadcast on the internet, and instructions on how to access will be sent closer to the call.

Nucor's Q2 Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates on Higher Prices
sum: Nucor Corporation NUE reported adjusted earnings of $4.84 per share for the second quarter of 2026. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.57. On a reported basis, earnings were $5.04 per share, up from $2.60 in the year-ago quarter.
The company recorded net sales of roughly $10.4 billion, up 23% year over year. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of roughly $10.06 billion.
Nucor Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Nucor Corporation Quote
Total sales tons to outside customers for steel mills in the second quarter were 5,659,000 tons, up 12% year over year and 1% sequentially. The figure surpassed our estimate of 5,621,000 tons.

Total sales tons to external customers increased 12% year over year to 7,605,000 tons. The external average sales price per ton rose 10% to $1,367. Overall operating rates at the company's steel mills were 91%, up from 85% in the second quarter of 2025 and 86% in the first quarter of 2026.

In the reported quarter, the Steel Mills segment posted earnings of $1.56 billion, up 84.6% from $843 million in the year-ago quarter. The improvement reflected higher average selling prices and volumes, along with a $130 million reduction in cost of products sold related to refunds for prior-period raw material procurement costs.
The Steel Products segment earned $353 million, down 9.9% from $392 million a year earlier. However, earnings improved sequentially on increased volumes and stable average realized pricing.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +5.91%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this steel company would post earnings of $2.79 per share when it actually produced earnings of $3.23, delivering a surprise of +15.77%.
Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

Nucor, which belongs to the Zacks Steel - Producers industry, posted revenues of $10.4 billion for the quarter ended June 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.34%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $8.46 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.
The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.
Nucor shares have added about 51.8% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 8.3%.
